Both Voyager spacecraft carried a gold-plated record. A committee chaired by Carl Sagan selected its contents for NASA: 115 analog images, natural sounds including surf and whale calls, musical selections spanning cultures and eras, and spoken greetings in 55 languages. Each record was protected by an aluminum jacket and accompanied by a cartridge and needle. Symbolic instructions explain the spacecraft's origin and how to play the record. The audio plays at 16 2/3 revolutions per minute.
Explore the Golden Record as both a collection of material from Earth and an object supplied with playback instructions.

For two months before May 18, 1980, Mount St. Helens experienced earthquakes and small explosions. On May 18 its steep north flank fell in a landslide, triggering a blast that traveled nearly horizontally before a powerful vertical eruption followed. The blast developed into a gravity-driven flow of hot material that felled millions of trees, stripped bark and branches, and scraped away soil in places.
Follow the north flank collapse and the documented direction and effects of the blast.

Jeweler Harry Winston donated the Hope Diamond to the Smithsonian in 1958. The 45.5-carat gem was sent from New York's General Post Office on November 8 by registered first-class mail in a plain brown package. Postage cost $2.44 and registration cost $142.85. It reached the Smithsonian on November 10 and was presented in a ceremony attended by Postmaster General Arthur Summerfield.
Tell the diamond's journey through the mail, from the New York post office to the Smithsonian presentation.

SOFAR stands for Sound Fixing and Ranging. This naturally occurring ocean channel allows low-frequency sound to travel long distances as sound waves bend up and down. Hydrophones at the channel's axis can detect faraway sounds, including whale calls. In some instances low-frequency sounds carry across entire ocean basins.
Explain how the ocean channel lets a hydrophone pick up distant whale calls. Keep the account to the mechanism and listening example.

Police raided the Stonewall Inn in the early hours of June 28, 1969. The raid prompted resistance and demonstrations continued on following nights in Christopher Park, across from the inn, and in the nearby neighborhood.
Locate the demonstrations in relation to the Stonewall Inn and Christopher Park using the limited event record.

The United States Congress passed the proposed 19th Amendment on June 4, 1919. It was ratified on August 18, 1920. The text bars the United States or any state from denying or abridging voting rights on account of sex.
Use the short timeline to explain the change established by the amendment's text.
